C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES.Name: Page width and tables: per-document typography, the titlebar quick-settings panel, and the honest three-mode table layout
C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES.Summary: Two intertwined product gaps become one change. (1) Page width is today an engineer-only setting — a free-text Appearance field (editorLineWidth, values like 720px or 80ch) with no menu, no shortcut, no canvas handle and no per-document value — while the editor already carries the full machinery for a first-class concept: the value is applied as the CSS variable --editorAreaWidth (util/theme.js:263, calc(100px + value)), consumed by muya's #ag-editor-id (muya/themes/default.css:166-173: max-width var(--editorAreaWidth), min-width 400px, padding 20/50/100/50), defaulted to 750px globally (renderer assets/styles/index.css:6) and re-declared by every one of the 34 shipped themes (uniform 750px today, ~line 90 of each *.theme.css), with the sidebar (C-40: 280 default, 220 min, live drag) as the only moving constraint on the canvas. (2) The table pill's "Fit to page" lies: it pins the frame to the text column while the content scrolls horizontally (tableResize/index.js:573 toggle, :318 autoFullWidth), so the label promises what the PDF path already delivers (print caps the article at 980px and wraps cells anywhere — printService.css:55, exportHtml.js:352) but the editor never shows. This change ships: a per-document width store (app-side, filePositionStore pattern, precedence document > theme > global, untitled documents follow the global default); a titlebar quick-settings button (chevrons-left-right glyph, next to the theme button) opening a mini-settings panel built from the real C-38 settings components in the neutral settings palette, with three live tabs — Page (per-unit presets ch 60/80/110 · px 600/750/900 · % 60/80/100 plus Full, a value stepper, unit conversion with 10% preset snapping and a nearest-preset anchor mark, font size 12-32, line height 1.2-2.0, a "for all documents" scope switch, a footer "Reset | Usual width: the current global default" and one export-connecting line), View (theme mode Auto/Light/Dark, the real 17-family swatch grid, and a per-document theme override switch), Tables (the default table mode and the sizes-memory switch); the honest three-mode table model — Auto (content), Fit page (smart proportional column distribution into the text column with wrap-anywhere fallback and, only when even minimal column sizes cannot fit, an explicit horizontal-scroll degradation with a "does not fit by N px" badge; the legacy fake-fit dies), and Full width redefined by the owner decision of 2026-10-25 as the whole window canvas (window minus sidebar, table escaping the text column, same smart distribution and the same scroll degradation); column sizes persisted as ratios plus px (migrating the px-only tableLayouts schema) so sizes survive window changes and travel across modes; drag affordances matching the real muya code — col-resize cursor (a shipped-code gap), live %·px size chips above columns during drag, and side-wall handles that stretch the whole table only outside Fit mode; and the supporting repairs surfaced by the research review: the dark-theme active-segment contrast fix in the shared settings components, the "Leave empty for full width" locale lie, and the columns-"sizes" terminology. The research base is the owner-iterated interactive mock cycle v1-v9 (nine review rounds with owner corrections) preserved as external owner working material; two consecutive clean corner-review passes over the research artifacts (mocks, fact base, doc consistency — 58 automated checks on two artifacts plus repository fact verification) were completed on 2026-10-25 before this spec was drafted, and this spec itself requires two consecutive clean reviews before it is proposed for owner approval.

Problem.Description: (1) Width is invisible: the only way to change the writing-area width is to know that Preferences → Appearance → Text → Line width accepts strings like "720px", "80ch" or "95%". There is no menu item, no shortcut, no per-document value, and the help text actively lies ("Leave empty for full width" — empty actually resolves to the theme default 750px, en.json:522). Meanwhile the product has already committed to a width opinion (EDITOR_IDEAL_CONTENT_WIDTH = 820 ≈ 80 chars, store/layout.js:11) and a dormant window auto-fit (F-WINDOW-AUTO-RESIZE) whose formula must integrate any per-document width. (2) The table mode named "Fit to page" does not fit: it only stops auto-expansion and lets content scroll, contradicting the label, the references (Word AutoFit Window, Google Docs, Notion all fit), and Mark's own print path (which does fit and wrap). Persisted column sizes are px-only (tableLayouts), so they cannot survive a different window, a zoom, a page-width change or a mode switch — the owner's original requirement was that sizes must work correctly in every table mode and transfer between them. (3) The UI surface question is settled by owner decision (mock v4-v9): controls live in the titlebar next to the theme button as a quick-settings panel; the panel must be built from the real settings design system (C-38 components and neutral palette), not new inventions; tabs must be live (Page / View / Tables); the button glyph is chevrons-left-right (<>), chosen by the owner for its double reading (stretch arrows / code). (4) Full width is redefined (owner, 2026-10-25): it means the whole window canvas, and when even minimal column sizes do not fit the window, the table degrades to horizontal column scrolling — scroll stops being a mode and becomes honest degradation, which retires the legacy fake-fit flag entirely.

Goals.R-1: Per-document page width store: an app-side store following the filePositionStore/tableLayoutStore pattern (per-file key, move-on-rename via the same rename flow, cap on file count, sanitize on read), holding width (value + unit ch/px/%) and, when R-4 is approved, the per-document theme override. Untitled documents carry no entry and resolve to the global preference. The stored value never mutates on transient clamping: the document keeps its setting; the rendered column is min(setting, canvas − indent) with the existing 400px floor, always centred in the current canvas.
Goals.R-2: Precedence and sources: effective width resolves document > theme > global. The panel and the inspector surface which source is active (mirroring the mock's source-naming pattern ("theme X (this file)")). The per-theme override mechanics already exist in code (every theme re-declares --editorAreaWidth; today all 34 say 750px), so "theme" precedence means themes may later ship different widths (C-50 territory, frozen — no theme ships a non-750 value in this change) while the document-level value wins over both.
Goals.R-3: Canvas model, one rule for text and tables: canvas = window − sidebar (shown/hidden/dragged; sidebar keeps 280 default / 220 min / no max, C-40). The text column and the Fit-page table frame both follow min(setting, canvas − indent); the % unit is the adaptive mode (a percentage of the canvas, following sidebar changes live). Reviving F-WINDOW-AUTO-RESIZE (separate follow-up) must use target = sidebar + effective page width instead of the hardcoded 820 — recorded here as a dependency so the formula is not re-hardcoded. The C-70 fullscreen table viewer keeps its own canvas: it ignores page width entirely, and Fit page remains its natural default — unchanged by this change.
Goals.R-4: Per-document theme override (owner gate №9): the View tab's "own theme for this file" switch pins the document to a family + mode member; the global titlebar cycle (Auto → Light → Dark, unchanged semantics) no longer affects a pinned document; the badge/inspector names the source. Recommendation: include in this change (the switch, the resolution order and the panel UI are already designed and mock-verified); the owner may defer it to a separate C-DOC-THEME — the plan records the decision either way. Separate per-table or per-diagram themes are explicitly rejected (owner gate №10, recommendation NO): one theme per document, everything inside follows it; diagram skins, if ever wanted, are a per-diagram block attribute (mermaid-style), never a document setting.
Goals.R-5: Titlebar quick-settings panel: a new titlebar button (chevrons-left-right, next to the theme button on macOS) opens a popover-panel that is a miniature of the real Settings window, built exclusively from the C-38 component set and the neutral settings palette (--pref* tokens, #ececec light / #242424 dark — the panel is not tinted by editor themes, and follows the theme mode light/dark member via a data-darkmode attribute). Three live tabs: Page, View, Tables. A footer row "Open Settings… ⌘," jumps to the real Settings window. The panel closes on outside click; interactions inside it never close it; no decorative chrome is allowed (the v5 lesson: quoted UI must be functional UI).
Goals.R-6: Page tab (the document typography triple — exactly the Appearance Text rows, per-document): Preset segmented control whose options depend on the unit (ch: 60/80/110 · px: 600/750/900 · %: 60/80/100, always plus Full window); value stepper with unit and per-unit bounds (ch 40-130, px 340-1100, % 40-100 — the mock-verified ranges); unit segmented (ch/px/%) that converts the current value and snaps to a preset within 10% (80 ch → 750 px → 80%), and when no preset matches exactly, the nearest preset carries a subtle accent underline so the current value always has a visual anchor; font size stepper (same value as ⌘+/⌘− zoom, ch measurements invariant) — bounds reconciliation is a plan-time item: the Settings range control caps at 12-32 while the C-49 unified zoom clamps to 12-36, and the panel must not introduce a third range (recommendation: one range, 12-36, applied to both surfaces); line height 1.2-2.0 (Settings range, step 0.1); "For all documents" scope switch (on writes the global default, off stores per-document); footer "Reset | Usual width: <the current global default>" (750 px today — the footer always names the live global default, never a hardcoded constant); one static connecting line "PDF export and printing print this same column; paper size and margins live in the print dialog" (no new export options — gate №11 accepted as designed).
Goals.R-7: View tab: theme mode segmented (Auto/Light/Dark — the titlebar cycle semantics), the family swatch grid of all 17 shipped families (two-half tiles with Aa + accent bar, selection ring, colours parsed from the shipped theme CSS — the themeSwatchColors approach, never a second palette table), and the R-4 per-document override switch with a help line naming the current scope. The Tables tab: default table mode segmented (Auto/Fit/Full — closes the C-65 NonGoal; today the muya option tableFullWidthDefault has no UI; owner gate №5 confirms the shipped default) and the "Remember column sizes" switch.
Goals.R-8: Honest table modes. Auto: content-sized frame (unchanged), wide tables scroll — GitHub-model. Fit page (new): the frame is the text column; columns are distributed by the smart algorithm (R-9); horizontal scroll only as explicit degradation. Full width (owner redefinition): the frame is the whole window canvas (window minus sidebar; the table escapes the text column; the page frame is unrestricted while the mode is active); the same smart distribution applies; the same degradation applies. The legacy "fit" flag (fake fit: pinned frame + scrolling content) is retired: stored fit:true entries migrate to the new Fit page (owner gate №4 recommendation), because the user intent ("keep it inside the column") is exactly what the new mode honestly delivers; the migration is one-directional and silent, switching back to Auto is one click.
Goals.R-9: Fit algorithm (shared by Fit page and Full width): for each column measure minContent (longest unbreakable token) and maxContent (longest cell line) over the header plus the first ~50 rows (cached, re-measured on structure change below the measured range). If Σmin ≤ W, distribute the free space proportionally to each column's slack (maxContent − minContent) capped at maxContent; leftover after all caps is split evenly (the CSS auto-layout / Word AutoFit Window behaviour). If Σmin > W, enable overflow-wrap: anywhere on cells and re-measure (the print-path precedent). If it still does not fit, degrade honestly: fix columns at minimal sizes, enable horizontal scrolling, show a "does not fit by N px — column scrolling instead of hiding data" badge; no truncation ellipses in the editor. Re-fit is debounced (~200 ms + rAF) on window resize, zoom, page-width change and column insert/delete. A user drag in Fit fixes that column and re-fits the remainder — the table never leaves its frame.
Goals.R-10: Column sizes persistence: tableLayouts entries gain ratios (fractions of table width), an explicit tableWidth (the side-wall-set width, null when unset — R-11) alongside widthsPx; drags write both; window/zoom/page-width changes and mode switches (Fit ↔ Full) re-apply ratios to the new width; Auto keeps ratios stored but unapplied (non-destructive, like today's dblclick reset); an inserted column gets a content-proportional share and the rest renormalize; header-signature identity (ordinal#signature) keeps today's reset-on-rename behaviour — improving ordinal-shift identity is explicitly deferred (gate №6). Export consumers finally get percentages: HTML col width, DOCX AutoFit Window (C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT follow-up), PDF prints as today. Two boundary behaviours are recorded as designed, not accidents: column sizes and the mode are not part of the markdown undo stack (unchanged from today), and a table pasted into another document starts fresh (new identity — sizes do not travel with the clipboard).
Goals.R-11: Table drag affordances (closing the gap between promise and muya code): col-resize cursor on column borders (the shipped code shows only the hairline — a real gap); during a drag, live size chips above every column ("40% · 222 px", theme-accent colour, fading shortly after release); side-wall handles on the table's outer edges, active only outside Fit mode, dragging sets an explicit table width (stored per table, double-click resets; dragging a wall in Full width switches the table to Auto with that width). Walls clamp inside the visible scroll area so the handle is always hittable.
Goals.R-12: Supporting repairs surfaced by the research review, shipped with this change: (a) dark-theme active-segment contrast in the shared settings components (the shipped #454545 tile on rgba(255,255,255,.08) is effectively invisible — raise the tile and add a hairline border, mirroring the mock's verified fix); (b) the "Leave empty for full width" locale lie (empty resolves to the theme default; either the text or the behaviour changes — recommendation: the text, since theme-default resolution is correct); (c) terminology: user-facing strings say "column sizes", not "column widths" (owner correction); (d) the sidebar note — no per-sidebar width variants exist, ever: one value, contextual clamp.
Goals.R-13: Surfacing beyond the panel: View → Page Width submenu (Compact 60 ch / Standard 80 ch — today's tuning / Wide 110 ch / Full window / Custom… opening the panel) with checkmarks following the effective value; the existing Appearance Line width textbox remains as the raw global field; no zoom-behaviour change (px values keep the column fixed, ch values scale with the font — the unit is always visible, so the cause is legible).
Goals.R-14: New governed module M-061 owns the page-width per-document store, the titlebar panel component boundary and the width-resolution pipeline; a matching verification anchor V-M-061 owns this change's commands, scenarios and content-free markers, both routed through the graph and verification indexes in the same bundle as the code. Existing anchors are not repurposed; the plan re-verifies both ids are still free before claiming them, and reconciles observed-write overlaps (notably C-50's frozen theme scope and the per-file store area shared with C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY / C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL) via grace lint --parallel-preflight before any write.
Goals.R-15: Owner decision gate — RESOLVED 2026-10-26: the owner accepted the spec for execution (owner quote, 2026-10-26: "consider it ready for execution"), confirming every recommendation below as designed (№1–№7, №9–№11; №7 stays one change; the plan pass is the next separate step with its own approval). Original gate text retained for traceability: the plan cannot start until every item below is either confirmed or flipped): №1 preset and unit values as designed; №2 app-side storage only (frontmatter pageWidth is a future option, not now); №3 precedence document > theme > global; №4 fit:true migrates to the new Fit page; №5 the default table mode setting ships with Auto default; №6 ordinal-shift identity deferred; №7 keep one change or split into C-PAGE-WIDTH + C-TABLE-FIT-PAGE at plan time (recommendation: one change, split only if parallel execution demands it — the shared canvas model couples them); №9 per-document theme override in or out (recommendation: in); №10 no separate table/diagram themes (recommendation: confirmed no); №11 the single export-connecting line as designed. The gate also records the research provenance: owner-iterated mock v1-v9, review-log with two consecutive clean corner passes (2026-10-25), preserved as owner-side working material outside the repository.

Constraints.Item: Language: every committed artifact of this change is English; the research mock and Russian working notes stay owner-side external material and are referenced by description, never by private absolute paths.

No product code in this pass: this bundle adds spec.xml only; plan.xml is a separate pass with its own owner approval (as in C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0). Implementation waves, corner matrix with verbatim Expected, and four-corner review passes (Correctness/Security/UX/Perf) belong to the plan.

Real design system only: the panel uses the shipped C-38 components and the neutral settings palette verbatim; any deviation (the dark-segment contrast fix, the tile metric compression) is declared in the plan and applied back to the shared components where it is a product fix, not forked into panel-local CSS.
The v5 lesson is binding: no decorative chrome. Every quoted control is functional; the five-tab Settings cosplay of mock v5 was rejected by the owner precisely because tabs without function confuse.

Table data is never hidden: degradation is horizontal scrolling with an explicit badge, never truncation, ellipsis or silent column clipping; the print path keeps its 980px cap and wrap-anywhere behaviour unchanged.

Zoom, sidebar, split-view and mobile respect one rule — the stored value never mutates on clamping; every surface recomputes min(setting, its canvas). The dormant F-WINDOW-AUTO-RESIZE is not revived here; its future formula (sidebar + effective page width) is recorded so it is not re-hardcoded to 820.

Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, the renderer suites, e2e; grace lint --assertions current shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline; observed-write overlaps with active changes (C-50 frozen theme scope, C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY, C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL, C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM) are sequenced or narrowed at plan time via grace lint --parallel-preflight, which is re-run, not trusted, before the first write.

No release or train admission follows from approval: this is product work; version bumps, tags and store uploads stay behind their separate owner release instruction. m048 build-mode notes apply where UI surfaces differ per channel (MAS/TestFlight/desktop).

NonGoals.NonGoal: The focus-mode panel variant (single-page popover without tabs): the owner chose tabs; the variant remains mock-side material only.
Separate per-table or per-diagram themes; any diagram skin system (per-diagram block attribute is a possible future change of its own, gated on real demand).
Page-as-paper model (A4/margins as document properties), print layout settings, or any new export options — the single connecting line in the Page tab is all the export coupling this change ships.
frontmatter pageWidth portability between machines; cloud sync of per-document settings.
Ordinal-shift table identity repair (gate №6), chunked/large-document rendering concerns (C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 owns that area), C-50 unfreezing or shipping non-750 theme widths.
Reviving F-WINDOW-AUTO-RESIZE; changing sidebar behaviour, limits or persistence (C-40 owns it).
Any change to the PDF/print rendering pipeline beyond what R-12's locale fix touches.
Creating plan.xml in this pass; implementing any R-item; claiming M-061/V-M-061 in the live graph before the plan confirms availability.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Per-document width: an entry survives rename (move follows the file), is absent for untitled documents, never mutates on clamping, and resolves document > theme > global with the active source named in the panel/inspector; the % unit follows canvas changes live; the 400px floor and centring hold on every surface (window resize, sidebar hide/show/drag, zoom).

Panel: opens from the titlebar chevrons-left-right button (next to theme on macOS), is built from C-38 components in the neutral palette, follows the light/dark theme mode (not the specific theme), keeps the dark-theme active segment clearly visible (contrast fix verified against the shipped palette), never closes on its own interactions, and its "Open Settings… ⌘," opens the real Settings window; preset sets switch with the unit; unit conversion snaps within 10% and the nearest preset always carries the anchor mark; the scope switch writes global vs per-document correctly.

View tab: all 17 families render as swatch tiles with colours parsed from the shipped theme CSS; Auto/Light/Dark follows the titlebar cycle semantics; the per-document override (if R-4 approved) pins the document against the global cycle with the source named; Tables tab sets the default mode and the sizes-memory switch.

Table modes: Fit page fits the text column with no horizontal scroll whenever Σmin allows (wrap fallback before degradation); Full width spans the whole window canvas and escapes the text column; degradation (minimal sizes + scroll + "does not fit by N px" badge, data never hidden) triggers only when the window itself cannot host the minima, identically in both modes; the legacy fake-fit flag no longer exists in code and stored fit:true entries open in the new Fit page.

Sizes: ratios + px persisted per table; drags write both; a resize/zoom/page-width/mode-switch re-applies ratios (Fit ↔ Full round-trip restores proportions); inserted columns renormalize; header-signature reset behaviour unchanged; the persisted store keeps the tableLayouts cap and sanitize rules.

Drag affordances: col-resize cursor on borders; size chips above every column during drag showing % and px, fading after release; side walls outside Fit set an explicit table width (double-click resets; Full → Auto transition on wall drag); walls remain hittable when the table overflows.

Supporting repairs: dark-segment contrast fixed in the shared components (not forked); the "Leave empty for full width" lie resolved; user-facing strings say "column sizes"; View → Page Width submenu items checkmark correctly and Custom… opens the panel.

Governance: M-061/V-M-061 routed in the same bundle as the code with content-free markers; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in touched files; locales updated in all ten languages as native copy; npm test and grace lint clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline; two consecutive clean review passes of this spec are recorded before owner approval is requested.
